_meta.note: Sector median P/E and EV/Revenue used for pricing score computation. Update by running scripts/update-sector-benchmarks.js or manually after quarterly earnings.

_unanchorableLayers._whyThisExists: v2.8.0 surfaced that 8 layers had no benchmark entry, so 24 tickers priced against the cross-industry default of forward PE 22 / EV-Revenue 5. Attempting to declare peers for all 8 established that 6 of them CANNOT be anchored, for reasons that are structural rather than effort-related. Recording the reason explicitly is worth more than a fabricated median: a placeholder is a visible 'unknown', whereas a wrong median is an invisible 'known'.
_unanchorableLayers._measuredHarm: The default is not neutral noise. Against forward PE 22 / EV-Rev 5, the affected tickers' actual ratios are extreme (APLD 234.7x / 40.9x, RKLB 2108x / 55.2x, ASTS -218x / 211.4x, WULF 84.9x / 69.0x, AXTI 53.5x / 32.2x). deviationToScore saturates at 5, so for most of these names BOTH the forwardPE and evRevenue components are pinned at 5.0 and 55% of pricingScore carries no information. This is structurally the SAME defect as the L6 single-member median found in v2.7.1, inverted: there the components were pinned at 3.0 (neutral), here they are pinned at 5.0 (maximally expensive).
_unanchorableLayers._consequence: Names in these layers can essentially only fail the pricing gate, EXCEPT where their real ratios happen to sit near 22/5 by coincidence. TTMI (19.9x / 4.34x), AVAV (34.4x / 4.04x), KTOS (43.6x / 5.65x) and CRCL (33.1x / 5.18x) currently PASS, and those passes rest on proximity to an arbitrary placeholder rather than on a sector comparison. Flagged for user decision; deliberately NOT auto-corrected, since changing it would move the PASS set.

layers.L11_FUEL: Insufficient valid sample, not absent peers. Exploration-stage uranium names (UEC, NXE, DNN) carry negative forward PE and EV/Revenue of 219x-605x on near-zero revenue — including them would make CCJ look arbitrarily cheap. Restricting to producers/processors leaves CCJ, LEU, UUUU: combined n=3, below the >=4 valid-names rule.
layers.L5_5: No comparable US-listed PCB/substrate manufacturer exists. Zhen Ding, Unimicron and Nan Ya are all Taiwan-listed and out of scope per v1.10. The available US names are EMS contract assemblers (BHE EV/Rev 1.05x, SANM 0.90x), which the v2.8.0 rule explicitly cites as a forbidden model mismatch — a contract assembler alongside a substrate fabricator produces a median describing no real company. NOTE: TTMI currently PASSES on the placeholder; a real PCB peer set does not exist to test that pass against.
layers.L8_OPT_MAT: Compound-semiconductor substrate peers are almost entirely non-US: Sumitomo and JX Metals (Japan OTC pink), IQE (UK), Soitec (France) — all out of scope per v1.10. The nearest US analogue, WOLF (SiC substrates), carries negative forward PE. Fewer than 2 valid external peers available.
layers.L_SPACE: forwardPE is meaningless for the constituents, not merely unanchored. RKLB prints 2108x and ASTS -218x because both are pre-profit; external peers are no better (RDW negative, PL 6099x). The EV/Revenue leg could be anchored (RDW 4.88x, IRDM 7.32x, VSAT 3.34x) but a half-anchored layer whose other half is nonsense is worse than an openly flagged placeholder.
layers.L_EMBI: The layer itself has no single business model, so no peer can match it. It holds a surgical-robotics firm (ISRG), a machine-vision firm (CGNX), an industrial motion supplier (PH), a carmaker (TSLA) and a sensor maker (VPG). Any median over that set describes no real company. This is a LAYER-DEFINITION problem, not a peer-selection problem — the fix is splitting the layer, which is a separate decision.
layers.L_DCOMP: Mixes two asset classes. Five constituents are crypto (RNDR, TAO, FIL, LINK, ETH) and are scored by update-crypto-valuations.js on P/Revenue and P/TVL, for which an equity forward-PE median is not merely wrong but categorically inapplicable. Only CRCL is an equity. An equity benchmark here would apply to exactly one ticker while sitting on a layer of five that must ignore it.

L9_MINER_CONVERT.label: Bitcoin Mining -> AI/HPC Conversion
L9_MINER_CONVERT._peerNote: Declared 2026-07-28. Five external comparables, all bitcoin miners at varying stages of HPC/AI conversion — the closest business-model match available and none of them universe members. CAVEAT ON THE forwardPE LEG: MARA, RIOT, CLSK and BTDR all carry NEGATIVE forward PE (loss-making), and median() filters non-positive values, so the forwardPE median rests on the profitable minority (CORZ plus whichever universe members are profitable). That is a selection bias toward the few winners in a mostly loss-making cohort. The EV/Revenue leg is sound: all five peers report valid positive ratios (5.97 to 21.83).

_changeLog.reason: Layer had NO benchmark entry, so all five members priced against the cross-industry default (forward PE 22 / EV-Rev 5). Declared five external bitcoin-miner peers.
_changeLog.observedDelta: APLD 3.5->3.5 | CIFR 3.7->2.8 FAIL->PASS | IREN 3.4->2.9 | WULF 3.6->3.0 | HUT 4.0->4.0. One funnel state flipped. THIS IS A METHODOLOGY EVENT, NOT A BUY SIGNAL — labelled per the v2.8.0 rule.
_changeLog.warning: The forwardPE median of 77.2 should NOT be read as 'the sector trades at 77x'. Loss-making peers (MARA, RIOT, CLSK, BTDR) are filtered out by median(), so the figure is the midpoint of the profitable minority, whose PEs are themselves extreme (CIFR 42x, CORZ 68x, WULF 85x, APLD 235x). Benchmarking against it says only 'cheap relative to other very expensive names'. CIFR's new PASS rests entirely on this leg and is low-confidence: pegRatio is N/A (the AXTI unmonitorable precedent), estimateRevision is -11.1% (consensus being marked DOWN, rare in this universe), and it sits exactly on the 2.8 entry threshold.

L_DEF.label: Defense Tech / Autonomous Systems
L_DEF._peerNote: Declared 2026-07-28. Three external comparables, meeting the >=2 floor with one to spare. BUSINESS-MODEL MISMATCH DISCLOSED per the v2.8.0 rule: the layer holds two mid-cap defense-tech names (AVAV ~$13B, KTOS) and no clean size-matched public peer set exists. LHX is ~4x larger and is a prime contractor rather than a systems specialist; RCAT is a direct product competitor in small military UAS but is loss-making, so it contributes only to the EV/Revenue leg. DRS is the closest match on both size and model. The median is therefore bracketed by a peer too large and a peer too small; treat it as advisory rather than precise.

_changeLog.reason: Layer had NO benchmark entry; both members priced against the default. Declared three external defense-tech peers.
_changeLog.observedDelta: AVAV 2.5->2.1 | KTOS 2.8->2.4. No funnel state flipped; both were passing and still pass, now with more headroom.
_changeLog.warning: Only 2 peers contribute a valid forwardPE (DRS 33.7, LHX 22.3) because RCAT is loss-making, so AVAV sits near the median and the self-reference the v2.8.0 rule targets is only partly removed here. Separately, both passes look weaker on delivery than on price: AVAV's +1y consensus EPS was revised DOWN 18% over 90 days with 1 of 4 quarters beating, and KTOS carries pegRatio 36.41.
